Valve Type and Design:
The valves are bolted bonnet steel gate valves with flanged and butt-welding ends.
The valves feature outside screw and yoke, rising stems, non-rising handwheels, single or double gate, wedge or parallel seating, metallic seating surfaces.
Pressure Class Designations: The valves are applicable to pressure class designations: 150, 300, 600, 900, 1500, 2500.
Application Context: The valves are intended for petroleum refinery and related applications where corrosion, erosion, and other service conditions require full port openings, heavy wall sections, and large stem diameters.
API Monogram and Licensing: If the product bears the API Monogram and is manufactured at a facility licensed by API, the requirements of Annex A apply.

Pressure/Temperature Ratings:
Pressure/temperature ratings shall be in accordance with those specified in the tables of ASME B16.34 for standard class for the applicable material specification and the applicable class.
Restrictions of temperature and concurrent pressure, or pressure and concurrent temperature, (e.g. those imposed by special soft seals or special trim materials), shall be marked on the valve identification plate (see Section 8).
The temperature for a corresponding pressure rating is the maximum temperature of the pressure-containing shell of the valve. In general, this temperature is the same as that of the contained fluid. The use of a pressure rating corresponding to a temperature other than that of the contained fluid is the responsibility of the user.
For temperatures below the lowest temperature listed in the pressure/temperature tables, the service pressure shall be no greater than the pressure for the lowest listed temperature. The use of valves at lower temperatures is the responsibility of the user. Consideration should be given to the loss of ductility and impact strength of many materials at low temperature.
Double seated valves, in some design configurations, may be capable of trapping liquid in the center cavity of the valve when in the closed position. If subjected to an increase in temperature, an excessive build-up of pressure can occur, which may result in a pressure boundary failure. Where such a condition is possible, it is the responsibility of the user to provide or require to be provided, means in design, installation, or operating procedure, to assure that the pressure in the valve does not exceed that allowed by this standard for the resultant temperature.

Welding Requirements for Flange to Valve:
Welding a flange to a valve body shall be by full penetration butt-welding.
Unless otherwise specified, attachment weld shall conform to ASME B31.3 or ISO 15649 for normal fluid service, including weld quality acceptance criteria and qualifications for the weld procedure and welder or welding operator.
Heat treatment shall be performed in accordance with Table 2.
Alignment Rings Usage: Integral or other alignment rings (centering backing rings) used to facilitate welding shall be removed after the weld is completed.
Butt-welding Ends Specifications:
Butt-welding ends for valve sizes greater than NPS 2 shall conform to the requirements of ASME B16.25 for the bore specified for use without backing rings.
Butt-welding ends for valves DN 50 (NPS 2) and smaller shall conform to the requirement of API 602.
Conversion of a flanged end valve to a butt-welding valve is not permitted except by agreement between the purchaser and manufacturer.
Chemical Composition Requirements for Ca:
The carbon content shall not exceed 0.23 % by mass.
The carbon equivalent, CE, shall not exceed 0.43 as determined by the following formula: CE = C + Mn/6 + (Cr + Mo + V)/5 + (Ni + Cu)/15.
C is weight % Carbon.
Mn is weight % Manganese.

Body Seat Dimensions:
The inside diameter of the seat opening shall not be less than that specified in ASME B16.34 for all Classes in sizes up to DN 600 (NPS 24).
The inside diameter of the seat opening shall not be less than that specified in ASME B16.34 for Classes 150 and 300 in sizes DN 650 to DN 750 (NPS 26 to NPS 30).
For Classes 150 and 300 in sizes DN 800 to DN 1050 (NPS 32 to NPS 42), the minimum inside diameter shall be as per Table 3.
Seating Surface Requirements:
Seating surfaces shall be integral or faced with weld metal.
Finished thickness of any facing material shall be not less than 1.6 mm (0.06 in.).
Austenitic Stainless Steel Valves:
Integral body seats are permitted in austenitic stainless steel valves.
When an austenitic stainless steel or a hardfacing material is used for the body seat, this material may be weld-deposited directly on the valve body.
Separate Seat Rings:
Separate seat rings shall be shoulder or bottom seated.
They shall be either threaded or seal welded in place.
For DN ≤ 50 (NPS ≤ 2), rolled or pressed in seat rings may be used.
Threaded seat rings shall be seal welded; tack welding or stitch welding is not permitted.
Seat Ring Surface and Edge Design:
Body seat rings shall have adequate seating area surface.
Edges shall be equipped with a radius or chamfer as necessary to prevent galling or any other damage to the disc when the valve is operated against pressure.
Assembly of Seat Rings:
Sealing compounds or greases shall not be used when assembling seat rings.
A light lubricant having a viscosity no greater than kerosene may be used to prevent galling of mating threaded surfaces.

Bonnet Flange Gasket Types:

For Class 150, the following are also acceptable: corrugated metal insert with graphite facings; when approved by the purchaser, flexible graphite sheet, reinforced with a stainless steel flat, perforated, tanged, or corrugated insert equipped with annular containment rings; when approved by the purchaser, other suitable facings may be used.

A two-piece split wedge gate or parallel seat double-disc gate may be furnished when specified by the purchaser.
A split wedge gate consists of two independent seating parts that conform to the body seats when closed.
The split wedge shall be designed so that the pieces cannot become separated, regardless of the gate position or valve orientation.
A double-disc gate has a spreading mechanism (i.e., a wedging device or spring) that forces the two parallel discs to the body seats when closed.
Gate Operation and Seat Clearance: Except for a double-disc gate, in the open position, the gate shall completely clear the valve seat openings.
Gate Guidance and Wear Prevention:
The body and gate shall have guide surfaces to minimize wear of the gate seats during operation of the valve, to accurately position the gate throughout the travel distance to its seat, and to ensure the alignment of the gate and stem in all orientations without gate binding or galling.
For sizes DN 650 (NPS 26) and above, as a minimum, wedge guides and body guides shall be hardfaced and machined with appropriate tolerances and clearances to allow for proper valve operation in any orientation, including effects of wear or galling.
Wedge guides and/or body guides shall not protrude beyond the seat rings into the port area of the valve.
The manufacturer shall provide in their installation and operation manual any operational limitations as a result of stem and valve orientation.

Wedge guides and/or body guides shall not protrude beyond the seat rings into the port area of the valve.

Packing Cross-Section: The packing may be square, rectangular or trapezoidal in cross-section.
Packing Nominal Radial Width: The nominal radial width of the packing, w, shall be in accordance with Table 6.
Packing Box Depth: The nominal depth of the packing box shall accommodate a minimum of five uncompressed rings of packing. Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, the packing box surface area in contact with the packing material shall have a surface finish, Ra, of 4.5 μm (175 μin.) or smoother.
Packing Box Bore Calculation: The nominal bore (inside diameter) of the packing box shall be the sum of the nominal valve stem diameter plus twice the nominal packing width plus a clearance factor, y, i.e. equal to dn + 2w + y. See Table 6 for the required values.
Gland and Gland Flange: A gland and a separate gland flange shall be provided for packing compression. The gland flange shall have two holes to receive the gland bolting. Slots for gland flange bolts shall not be used. The gland and gland flange shall be self-aligning. The gland shall have a shoulder at its outer edge so as to prevent complete entry of the gland into the packing box.
Lantern Ring Provision: A lantern ring shall be provided only if so specified by the purchaser. In order to accommodate the lantern ring, the packing box depth shall be at least equivalent to that of a minimum of three uncompressed rings of packing above the lantern ring and three uncompressed rings of packing below the lantern ring plus the length of the lantern ring.
Clearance Between Packing Box Bore and G: The clearance between the packing box bore (inside diameter) and the outside diameter of the gland (see Figure C.1) shall be nominally less than the diametrical clearance between the inside diameter of the gland and the stem diameter.
Valve Type Testing: Valves shall be qualified by type testing to meet the fugitive emissions requirements of API Std. 624.
Bolting Standards:
Bolting shall be standard inch series bolting, except if the purchaser specifies metric series bolting.
Bolting for the bonnet-to-body joint shall be continuously threaded stud bolts with heavy, semi-finished hexagon nuts that are in accordance with ASME B18.2.2 or ASME B18.2.6M.
Yoke-to-bonnet bolting shall be either continuously threaded stud bolts or headed bolts with hexagon nuts.
Gland bolts shall be hinged eyebolts, headed bolts, stud bolts or studs. Hexagon nuts shall be used.
Bolting with diameters 25 mm (1 in.) and smaller shall have coarse (UNC) threads or the most nearly corresponding metric threads.
Bolting with diameters larger than 25 mm (1 in.) shall be 8-thread series (8UN) or the most nearly corresponding metric threads.
Bolt threads shall be Class 2A and nut threads shall be Class 2B, in accordance with ASME B1.1.
Studs used for gland bolting shall use a Class 5 interference fit conforming to ASME B1.12.
When metric bolting is used, metric bolt threads shall be tolerance Class 6g and nuts tolerance Class 6H in accordance with ASME B1.13M.
Handwheel Specifications:
Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, the valve shall be supplied with a direct operated handwheel that opens the valve when turned in a counter-clockwise direction.
The handwheel shall be a spoke-rim type with a maximum of six spokes and shall be free from burrs and sharp edges.
Unless otherwise specified, the handwheel shall be a one-piece casting or forging or a multi-piece carbon steel fabrication that includes other carbon steel product forms.
Fabricated handwheels shall have strength and toughness characteristics comparable to that of handwheels made as one-piece castings or forgings.
The handwheel shall be marked with the word “OPEN” and an arrow pointing in the direction of opening, except when the handwheel size makes such marking impractical.
The handwheel shall be retained on the stem nut by a threaded handwheel nut.
Flange Mating Dimensions: Valve-to-gear-box or power actuator flange mating dimensions shall be according to ISO 5210 or MSS SP-102, or shall comply with the purchaser’s specifications.

The design and construction of the joint and the piping of auxiliary connections shall conform to the requirements of ASME B16.34.
When required for valve DN 50 (NPS 2) or larger, auxiliary connections shall be sized and located as specified in ASME B16.34.
The size and location of auxiliary connections shall be indicated on the purchase order.

Gate material shall be steel, at least equal in corrosion resistance to that of the body material.
Yoke, separate material shall be carbon steel or same material group as the bonnet.
Bolting material for body to bonnet shall be as listed in Annex D unless otherwise agreed; for service temperatures below –29 °C (–20 °F) or above 454 °C (850 °F), the purchase order shall specify the bolting material.

Gland flange material shall be steel.
Gland material shall have melting point above 955 °C (1750 °F).
Packing shall be suitable for steam and petroleum fluids for temperature range from –29 °C to 538 °C (–20 °F to 1000 °F), and shall contain a corrosion inhibitor.
Lantern ring or spacer ring material shall have corrosion resistance at least equal to that of the body material.
Stem nut material shall be austenitic ductile iron or copper alloy with melting point above 955 °C (1750 °F).
Handwheel material shall be malleable iron, carbon steel, or ductile iron.
Handwheel nut (retaining) material shall be steel, malleable iron, ductile iron, or non-ferrous copper alloy.
Pipe plugs nominal composition shall be the same as the shell material; cast iron plugs shall not be used.
Bypass piping and valves nominal composition shall be the same as the shell material.
Pin, double disk stem to gate material shall be austenitic stainless steel.
Identification plate material shall be austenitic stainless steel or nickel alloy, attached to the valve by corrosion-resistant fasteners or by welding.

Valve Marking Requirements:
Valves shall be marked in accordance with ASME B16.34, with the additional designation 'API 600' on the nameplate.
Unidirectional valves shall be marked with a flow direction arrow cast, forged, or stamped into the valve body outer wall, or with a separate identification plate permanently attached to the body indicating the permitted flow direction.
Coating Requirements for Valve Surfaces:
Unmachined exterior surfaces of the shell shall be painted per the manufacturer’s standard paint with an aluminum or silver color, except for austenitic stainless steel valves which shall not be painted.
Machined or threaded surfaces (excluding those on austenitic stainless steel materials) shall be coated with an easily removable rust preventative. The stem does not need coating if the stem packing contains a corrosion inhibitor.
Valve End Flange and Welding End Protect:
Valve end flanges and welding ends shall be blanked to protect gasket surfaces and valve internals during shipment and storage.
Protective covers shall be made of wood, wood fiber, plastic, or metal and securely attached using bolts, steel straps, steel clips, or suitable friction-locking devices.
Protective covers shall be designed so that the valve cannot be installed without removal of the cover.
Tapped Connection Protection:
Tapped connections shall be fitted with fully tightened and sealed threaded plugs.
The material of the plugs for tapped connections shall have the same nominal chemical composition as the shell material as specified in section 5.12.
Gate Position for Shipment:
The valve shall be shipped with the gate closed.
The valve shall be shipped with the lantern ring, if specified, and the packing installed.
The remaining adjustment length of the packing gland at the time of shipment, with the gland tight, shall be greater than one-and-one half times the packing width specified in Table 6.
Stem Packing Requirements:
The valve shall be shipped with the lantern ring, if specified, and the packing installed.
The remaining adjustment length of the packing gland at the time of shipment, with the gland tight, shall be greater than one-and-one half times the packing width specified in Table 6.
Packaging Specifications:
Unless export packaging is specified in the purchase order, valves may be shipped loose, palletized, or packed in a box or crate.
When export packaging is specified in the purchase order, valves shall be shipped individually or collectively in wooden boxes or crates in a manner that will prevent shifting within the package.

The marking procedure shall define the authority responsible for application and removal of the API Monogram and license number.
The marking procedure shall define the method(s) used to apply the Monogram and license number.
The marking procedure shall identify the location on the product where the API Monogram and license number are to be applied.
The marking procedure shall require the application of the date of manufacture of the product in conjunction with the use of the API Monogram and license number.

The marking procedure shall define the application of all other required API product specification(s) and/or standard(s) marking requirements.
Only an API licensee shall apply the API Monogram and its designated license number to API monogrammable products.
The API Monogram and license number, when issued, are site-specific and shall only be applied at that site-specific licensed facility location.
The API Monogram may be applied at any time appropriate during the production process but shall be removed in accordance with the licensee's API Monogram marking procedure if the product is subsequently found to be out of conformance with any of the requirements of the applicable API product specification(s) and/or standard(s) and API Monogram Program.

Each licensee and/or applicant for licensing shall maintain current design documentation as identified in API Q1 for all of the applicable products that fall under the scope of each Monogram license.

Unless otherwise specified, reference to the API specifications and/or standards shall be, as a minimum, "API [Document Number]" (e.g. API 6A, or API 600).
Unless otherwise specified, when space allows, the marking may include use of "Spec" or "Std", as applicable (e.g. API Spec 6A or API Std 600).
Units for Product Marking:
Products shall be marked with units as specified in the API specification and/or standard.
If not specified, equipment shall be marked with U.S. customary (USC) units.
Use of dual units [USC units and metric (SI) units] may be acceptable, if such units are allowed by the applicable product specification and/or standard.
Nameplates, when applicable, shall be made of a corrosion-resistant material unless otherwise specified by the API specification and/or standard.
Nameplate shall be located as specified by the API specification and/or standard.
If the location is not specified, then the licensee shall develop and maintain a procedure detailing the location to which the nameplate shall be applied.
Nameplates may be attached at any time during the manufacturing process.
Nameplate Requirements:
Nameplates, when applicable, shall be made of a corrosion-resistant material unless otherwise specified by the API specification and/or standard.
Nameplate shall be located as specified by the API specification and/or standard.
If the location is not specified, then the licensee shall develop and maintain a procedure detailing the location to which the nameplate shall be applied.
Nameplates may be attached at any time during the manufacturing process.
The API Monogram and license number shall be marked on the nameplate, in addition to the other product marking requirements specified by the applicable product specification and/or standard.
License Number Usage:
The API Monogram license number shall not be used unless it is marked in conjunction with the API Monogram.
The license number shall be used in close proximity to the API Monogram.
Nonconformance Reporting:
API solicits information on products that are found to be nonconforming with API specified requirements, as well as field failures (or malfunctions), which are judged to be caused by either specification and/or standard deficiencies or nonconformities against API specified requirements.
Customers are requested to report to API all problems with API monogrammed products.
A nonconformance may be reported using the API Nonconformance Reporting System available at http://compositelist.api.org/ncr.aspx.
